fruits.extendedStory: Find those porters on the entrance door. Two bronze figures of the bastaixos are set into it, in memory of the neighbourhood's guilds. Now search the windows for something odder: a small leaded pane with a football crest. When the windows were replaced, the church looked for sponsors, and FC Barcelona paid for this one, its badge the signature. The church took just fifty-four years to finish, when buildings of this kind often took more than a century.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Such diese Träger an der Eingangstür. Zwei Bronzefiguren der Bastaixos sind dort eingelassen, zur Erinnerung an die Zünfte des Viertels. Dann such in den Fenstern etwas noch Seltsameres: eine kleine Bleiglasscheibe mit einem Fußballwappen. Als die Fenster ersetzt wurden, suchte die Kirche Sponsoren, und der FC Barcelona bezahlte diese Scheibe, mit seinem Wappen als Unterschrift. Nur vierundfünfzig Jahre dauerte der Bau, während solche Bauten oft über ein Jahrhundert brauchten.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Find those porters on the entrance door. Two bronze figures of the bastaixos are set into it, in memory of the neighbourhood's guilds. Now search the windows for something odder: a small leaded pane with a football crest. When the windows were replaced, the church looked for sponsors, and FC Barcelona paid for this one, its badge the signature. The church took just fifty-four years to finish, when buildings of this kind often took more than a century.

localizedStory.de: Der Legende nach hat diese Kirche so viele Steine, wie ihr Bau Tage brauchte, und die Hafenträger trugen sie vom Montjuïc herüber.
localizedStory.en: Legend says this church has as many stones as it took days to build, stones the harbour porters carried from Montjuïc.

fruits.name: Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar
fruits.story: Legend says this church has as many stones as it took days to build, stones the harbour porters carried from Montjuïc.

fruits.extendedStory: This museum began with a friend: Jaume Sabartés, Picasso's secretary, started talks to give his private collection to the city. Picasso had vowed not to set foot in Spain while there was a dictator, yet he wanted a Picasso museum in Barcelona. So he ran the refit of this palace from France, with photographs sent to him regularly. It opened as the Sabartés Collection, not under Picasso's name, because of his differences with the Franco regime. Later he gave it fifty-eight paintings, forty-four of them variations on Velázquez's Las Meninas.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Dieses Museum begann mit einem Freund: Jaume Sabartés, Picassos Sekretär, leitete die Gespräche ein, um der Stadt seine Privatsammlung zu schenken. Picasso hatte geschworen, Spanien unter einem Diktator nicht zu betreten, doch ein Picasso-Museum in Barcelona wollte er. Also leitete er den Umbau dieses Palasts von Frankreich aus, mit Fotos, die man ihm regelmäßig schickte. Es eröffnete als Sammlung Sabartés, nicht unter Picassos Namen, wegen seiner Differenzen mit dem Franco-Regime. Später schenkte er ihm achtundfünfzig Gemälde, vierundvierzig davon Variationen auf Las Meninas von Velázquez.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This museum began with a friend: Jaume Sabartés, Picasso's secretary, started talks to give his private collection to the city. Picasso had vowed not to set foot in Spain while there was a dictator, yet he wanted a Picasso museum in Barcelona. So he ran the refit of this palace from France, with photographs sent to him regularly. It opened as the Sabartés Collection, not under Picasso's name, because of his differences with the Franco regime. Later he gave it fifty-eight paintings, forty-four of them variations on Velázquez's Las Meninas.

localizedStory.de: Man erzählt, Picasso habe seine Armut versteckt: Er malte Möbel, Obst, Münzen und ein Dienstmädchen an die Wände seiner Wohnung in Barcelona.
localizedStory.en: The story goes that Picasso hid his poverty by painting furniture, fruit, coins and a maid on a bare Barcelona flat's walls.

fruits.name: Museu Picasso
fruits.story: The story goes that Picasso hid his poverty by painting furniture, fruit, coins and a maid on a bare Barcelona flat's walls.

fruits.extendedStory: The cathedral's tradition says the Holy Christ of Lepanto sailed on the flagship at that sea battle. Two tales explain why the carved body leans. In one it swerved to dodge a cannonball, in the other it bent to plug a hole in the hull. Next door, on the Casa de l'Ardiaca, once let to the city's lawyers, find the letterbox with a tortoise and swallows. The story told is that the tortoise shows how slow justice is, and the swallows how fast it ought to be.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Überlieferung der Kathedrale nach fuhr der Heilige Christus von Lepanto in jener Seeschlacht auf dem Flaggschiff mit. Zwei Erzählungen erklären, warum sich der geschnitzte Körper neigt. In der einen wich er einer Kanonenkugel aus, in der anderen stopfte er ein Loch im Rumpf. Gleich nebenan, an der Casa de l'Ardiaca, einst an die Anwälte der Stadt vermietet, findest du den Briefkasten mit Schildkröte und Schwalben. Man erzählt, die Schildkröte zeige, wie langsam die Justiz ist, und die Schwalben, wie schnell sie sein sollte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The cathedral's tradition says the Holy Christ of Lepanto sailed on the flagship at that sea battle. Two tales explain why the carved body leans. In one it swerved to dodge a cannonball, in the other it bent to plug a hole in the hull. Next door, on the Casa de l'Ardiaca, once let to the city's lawyers, find the letterbox with a tortoise and swallows. The story told is that the tortoise shows how slow justice is, and the swallows how fast it ought to be.

localizedStory.de: Im Kreuzgang dieser Kathedrale leben dreizehn Gänse. Der Legende nach war die heilige Eulàlia, das Gänsemädchen in ihrem Namen, ebenso viele Jahre alt.
localizedStory.en: Thirteen geese live in this cathedral's cloister. Legend says Saint Eulàlia, the goose-herding girl in its name, was just that many years old.

fruits.name: Catedral de la Santa Creu i Santa Eulàlia
fruits.story: Thirteen geese live in this cathedral's cloister. Legend says Saint Eulàlia, the goose-herding girl in its name, was just that many years old.

fruits.extendedStory: Inside, around the stage, stand eighteen young women known as the muses, each playing a different instrument. Their upper bodies stick out of the wall as sculpture, and their lower bodies are mosaic set in it. A choir drove this building, the Orfeó Català, and the public paid for it by subscription. On Saint Stephen's Day, the day after Christmas, that choir gives a concert here that Barcelona counts as part of the holiday. And everyone coming to concerts, from every part of society, shared one grand staircase.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Drinnen stehen rund um die Bühne achtzehn junge Frauen, genannt die Musen, und jede spielt ein anderes Instrument. Ihr Oberkörper ragt als Skulptur aus der Wand, ihr Unterkörper ist Mosaik in der Wand. Ein Chor trieb den Bau voran, das Orfeó Català, und die Öffentlichkeit bezahlte ihn per Subskription. Am Stephanstag, dem Tag nach Weihnachten, gibt dieser Chor hier ein Konzert, das für Barcelona zum Feiertag gehört. Und alle, die zu den Konzerten kamen, aus jeder Schicht, teilten sich eine große Treppe.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Inside, around the stage, stand eighteen young women known as the muses, each playing a different instrument. Their upper bodies stick out of the wall as sculpture, and their lower bodies are mosaic set in it. A choir drove this building, the Orfeó Català, and the public paid for it by subscription. On Saint Stephen's Day, the day after Christmas, that choir gives a concert here that Barcelona counts as part of the holiday. And everyone coming to concerts, from every part of society, shared one grand staircase.

localizedStory.de: Der Pianist Keith Jarrett, so heißt es, wollte hier an einem Sonntag nur auf schwarzem Teppich spielen. Das Personal, erzählt man, zerschnitt stattdessen einen Vorhang.
localizedStory.en: Pianist Keith Jarrett, the story goes, refused a Sunday concert here without a black carpet. Staff, it is said, cut up a curtain instead.

fruits.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
fruits.story: Pianist Keith Jarrett, the story goes, refused a Sunday concert here without a black carpet. Staff, it is said, cut up a curtain instead.

fruits.extendedStory: The legend's source, it is said, is a city gate where the fountain once stood and people came looking for temporary work. They drank while they waited, so the tale goes, and always came back to look for more. Barça fans gather at this fountain to celebrate titles, a habit from 1930, when a newspaper posted results in its window. People say a river called Malla once ran here. A geographer, Pau Vila, suspected there never was one, and that people had misread the word rambla, a usually dry stream.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Ursprung, so heißt es, liegt an einem Stadttor, vor dem der Brunnen einst stand und wo Leute Gelegenheitsarbeit suchten. Sie tranken beim Warten, erzählt man, und kamen immer wieder, um nach mehr zu suchen. Barça-Fans treffen sich an diesem Brunnen, um Titel zu feiern, seit 1930 eine Zeitung die Ergebnisse in ihrem Fenster aushängte. Man sagt, hier sei einst ein Fluss namens Malla geflossen. Der Geograph Pau Vila vermutete, dass es ihn nie gab und dass man das Wort Rambla falsch las, ein meist trockenes Bachbett.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The legend's source, it is said, is a city gate where the fountain once stood and people came looking for temporary work. They drank while they waited, so the tale goes, and always came back to look for more. Barça fans gather at this fountain to celebrate titles, a habit from 1930, when a newspaper posted results in its window. People say a river called Malla once ran here. A geographer, Pau Vila, suspected there never was one, and that people had misread the word rambla, a usually dry stream.

localizedStory.de: Der Legende nach kehrt immer wieder nach Barcelona zurück, wer aus dem eisernen Font de Canaletes oben an dieser Rambla trinkt.
localizedStory.en: Legend says whoever drinks from the iron Font de Canaletes, at the top of this Rambla, will always return to Barcelona.

fruits.name: La Rambla
fruits.story: Legend says whoever drinks from the iron Font de Canaletes, at the top of this Rambla, will always return to Barcelona.

fruits.extendedStory: A members' society, the Ateneu, bought the palace in 1905 and wanted a lift as a symbol of modernity. Its board made the engineer follow its own drawing: a mahogany box under a stained-glass dome. One member used to bring his monkey and let it climb the palms. And for Corpus, the garden joins the custom of the dancing egg, balanced on a fountain's jet. Some say it stands for the burst of spring.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Eine Mitgliedergesellschaft, das Ateneu, kaufte den Palast 1905 und wollte einen Aufzug als Zeichen der Moderne. Der Vorstand ließ den Ingenieur nach eigener Zeichnung bauen: eine Kabine aus Mahagoni unter einer Buntglaskuppel. Ein Mitglied brachte oft seinen Affen mit und ließ ihn auf die Palmen klettern. Und zu Fronleichnam macht der Garten beim Brauch des tanzenden Eis mit, das auf dem Strahl eines Brunnens balanciert. Es stehe für den Frühling, heißt es.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A members' society, the Ateneu, bought the palace in 1905 and wanted a lift as a symbol of modernity. Its board made the engineer follow its own drawing: a mahogany box under a stained-glass dome. One member used to bring his monkey and let it climb the palms. And for Corpus, the garden joins the custom of the dancing egg, balanced on a fountain's jet. Some say it stands for the burst of spring.

localizedStory.de: Katzen hielten einst die Ratten von der Bibliothek dieses Palasts fern. Die letzten drei, Neró, Apolo und Diana, lebten bis nach 2000 in den Lesesälen.
localizedStory.en: Cats once guarded this palace's library from rats. The last three, Neró, Apolo and Diana, lived in the reading rooms until after 2000.

fruits.name: Palau Savassona
fruits.story: Cats once guarded this palace's library from rats. The last three, Neró, Apolo and Diana, lived in the reading rooms until after 2000.

fruits.extendedStory: Macià led Catalonia's government for three years, and three steps set into the pedestal count them. Underfoot, look for the compass rose among the pigeons, on ground where a horse circus once played. The street leaving the square, Portal de l'Àngel, has its own tale. The story goes that its old wall gate got the name when Saint Vincent Ferrer stopped there. A mighty angel appeared, it is said, guarding the city by order of God.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Macià führte drei Jahre lang die Regierung Kataloniens, und drei Stufen im Sockel zählen sie. Zu deinen Füßen findest du die Windrose zwischen den Tauben, auf einem Boden, wo einst ein Pferdezirkus spielte. Die Straße, die vom Platz abgeht, das Portal de l'Àngel, hat ihre eigene Geschichte. Der Sage nach bekam ihr altes Stadttor den Namen, als der heilige Vinzenz Ferrer dort anhielt. Ein mächtiger Engel erschien, heißt es, und bewachte die Stadt in Gottes Auftrag.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Macià led Catalonia's government for three years, and three steps set into the pedestal count them. Underfoot, look for the compass rose among the pigeons, on ground where a horse circus once played. The street leaving the square, Portal de l'Àngel, has its own tale. The story goes that its old wall gate got the name when Saint Vincent Ferrer stopped there. A mighty angel appeared, it is said, guarding the city by order of God.

localizedStory.de: Such eine Treppe, die kopfsteht: das Denkmal für Francesc Macià. Ihre Stufen enden abrupt, für eine Zukunft, die noch gebaut wird.
localizedStory.en: Look for a staircase standing upside down. It is the monument to Francesc Macià, and its steps stop short, for a future still being built.

fruits.name: Plaça de Catalunya
fruits.story: Look for a staircase standing upside down. It is the monument to Francesc Macià, and its steps stop short, for a future still being built.

fruits.extendedStory: The tale gives the idea to a humble shepherd, with bundles of wood tied to the goats' horns. They were let loose at night, so the tale goes, and the men took them for a great force climbing up. That, it is said, is why the place was called Centelles: cent teies, a hundred torches. Here, Lluís de Centelles bought two houses on this corner and built his new home from the foundations up. From 1847 the city's Philharmonic Society had a great concert hall on its main floor.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Idee, erzählt man, hatte ein einfacher Hirte: Holzbündel an den Hörnern der Ziegen. Nachts ließ man sie los, heißt es, und die Männer hielten sie für eine große Streitmacht, die heraufkam. Darum, so die Geschichte, hieß der Ort fortan Centelles: cent teies, hundert Fackeln. Hier kaufte Lluís de Centelles zwei Häuser an dieser Ecke und baute sich von den Fundamenten an ein neues Heim. Ab 1847 hatte die Philharmonische Gesellschaft der Stadt im Hauptgeschoss einen großen Konzertsaal.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tale gives the idea to a humble shepherd, with bundles of wood tied to the goats' horns. They were let loose at night, so the tale goes, and the men took them for a great force climbing up. That, it is said, is why the place was called Centelles: cent teies, a hundred torches. Here, Lluís de Centelles bought two houses on this corner and built his new home from the foundations up. From 1847 the city's Philharmonic Society had a great concert hall on its main floor.

localizedStory.de: Die Centelles bauten dieses Haus. Auf ihrer Burg, so die Geschichte, vertrieben fünfzig Ziegen mit Fackeln an den Hörnern die Männer, die sie hielten.
localizedStory.en: The Centelles built this house. At their castle, the story goes, fifty goats with torches on their horns scared off the men holding it.

fruits.name: Palau Centelles
fruits.story: The Centelles built this house. At their castle, the story goes, fifty goats with torches on their horns scared off the men holding it.

fruits.extendedStory: The job had gone to a decorator, Jaume Serra Givert, who died before doing it. Gaudí's old teacher, Joan Martorell, talked the council into handing it to Gaudí. Gaudí ordered the six arms painted red, so the glare on black iron would not blur their shape. And the square is not square: one side has one more arcade than the others. Debates on any subject once sprang up here, in circles nicknamed the Barcelona Hyde Park.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Den Auftrag hatte ein Dekorateur, Jaume Serra Givert, der starb, bevor er ihn ausführen konnte. Gaudís alter Lehrer Joan Martorell überredete den Stadtrat, ihn Gaudí zu geben. Gaudí ließ die sechs Arme rot streichen, damit das grelle Licht auf schwarzem Eisen ihre Form nicht verwischt. Und der Platz ist gar nicht quadratisch: Eine Seite hat eine Arkade mehr als die anderen. Früher entstanden hier spontane Runden, die über alles debattierten, ihr Spitzname: der Hyde Park von Barcelona.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The job had gone to a decorator, Jaume Serra Givert, who died before doing it. Gaudí's old teacher, Joan Martorell, talked the council into handing it to Gaudí. Gaudí ordered the six arms painted red, so the glare on black iron would not blur their shape. And the square is not square: one side has one more arcade than the others. Debates on any subject once sprang up here, in circles nicknamed the Barcelona Hyde Park.

localizedStory.de: Gaudí bekam den Laternen-Auftrag hier, bevor er überhaupt den Architektentitel hatte. Such die zwei Laternen unter dem Flügelhelm des Merkur.
localizedStory.en: Gaudí got the lamp job here before he even held his architect's title. Look for the two lamp-posts under Mercury's winged helmet.

fruits.name: Plaça Reial
